topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s aims and introduces the hallmark framework that will organise the discussion.

topics.label: Signalling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Disrupted differentiation in blood and intestinal cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how altered differentiation affects cancer-cell maturity and tissue organisation.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells evade mitochondrial apoptosis by altering p53 activity or the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and normal stress-response safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the safeguards that limit continued cell proliferation and how cancer-associated mutations overcome them, concluding the discussion of mutation-driven growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered metabolism supports cancer and interacts with the molecular changes that drive it.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as support for tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumours recruit a vascular supply through the angiogenic switch to sustain their growth.

topics.label: Metastatic spread and successful growth at secondary sites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what enables disseminating cancer cells to establish secondary tumours and how that process can be detected and investigated.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by revisiting its central message and learning goals, recommending further reading and inviting questions.
